Born and raised in a small coastal town, I was the youngest of three siblings. My parents were both hardworking individuals who instilled in me the value of responsibility and determination. Despite our family's financial struggles, they made sure we never felt deprived of love and support.

Growing up, I was always drawn to the ocean. Its vastness and mystery fascinated me. I spent countless hours by the shore, observing the waves, the marine life, and the ever-changing weather patterns. This early exposure to nature shaped my appreciation for the environment and sparked my interest in marine biology.

In school, I was an average student, but I excelled in science subjects. Teachers often praised my curiosity and eagerness to learn. Outside of academics, I was part of various extracurricular activities, including the debate team and the school newspaper. These experiences helped me develop strong communication skills and a knack for storytelling.

After high school, I enrolled in a local university to pursue a degree in Marine Biology. During my undergraduate years, I participated in several research projects, honing my analytical and problem-solving abilities. My professors recognized my potential and offered me opportunities to assist in teaching introductory courses. This experience solidified my passion for sharing knowledge and inspired me to consider a career in education.

Post-graduation, I worked as a research assistant at a renowned marine laboratory. Here, I contributed to significant discoveries concerning ocean acidification and its impact on coral reefs. Although the work was challenging, I thrived in the collaborative environment and enjoyed the satisfaction of making a tangible difference.

A few years later, I decided to further my studies and applied for a master's program in Environmental Education. My goal was to combine my expertise in marine biology with my love for teaching. The program challenged me intellectually and emotionally, pushing me beyond my comfort zone. However, I persevered and emerged more resilient and committed than ever.

Today, I am proud to say that I am a Marine Science Educator, sharing my passion and knowledge with students from diverse backgrounds. In addition to teaching, I also conduct workshops for educators, advocating for inclusive and engaging learning environments. Reflecting on my journey, I am grateful for the opportunities I've had and the challenges I've overcome. Every step has been instrumental in shaping me into the person I am today.
